author: Awen
text:
Issue with drawing on map with Steam overlay
Noticed something odd a few days ago, when drawing on the map, entire game begins to stutter and drawing is interrupted. For example, if you right click to draw and just slowly move the mouse across the screen to make a line, there will be intermittent gaps in the drawn line without ever releasing the mouse button. I'm on the beta branch, and never noticed this before. I don't believe there has been any updates in a while. Work arounds I've found: Option 1: Turning off the Steam overlay. This completely resolves the drawing issue, however it also breaks the in game "invite" button on multiplayer. It throws a little warning when pressing invite now, saying the functionality is disabled with the overlay off and invites will have to be initiated via the Steam client instead. Option 2: Change the drawing mode. Instead of holding right click to draw, you can toggle on drawing from the icon in the bottom left, once toggled you now draw by holding down LEFT click. This method has no issues with the overlay on.

author: Adrian
text:
How did you screw up this badly?
Spire 1 was a fantastic game. 2 is currently garbage. There is absolutely no consistency in enemy structure and you've chosen to add "cheats" for the enemies to produce artificial difficulty The Waterfall Giant is a perfect example -- it has a strength mechanism based on it's steam explosion counter, which cannot be effected in any way. You have a mechanism for that, it's called strength. You chose to hide the mechanic to make it harder for players -- not because they lack strategy, but because you were too lazy to make a fight legitimately difficult. Cut this ♥♥♥♥ out and get back to proper gameplay. If you want a stats based combat game you have to base the combats on stats. You wouldn't think I'd have to explain that.

author: Vachu
text:
I wish the devs tried to manage expectations better
Maybe I've been spoiled in the past, but I got one of my favorite game, Factorio, very early in its early access phase and for me this was the right way to do it : Friday Facts. Every friday, the devs posted about anything related to development. Sometimes it was about a change in the engine, a tough optimization from a coder, some thoughts on trying new art, etc. It was very varied and it was always nice to know what was going on behind the scenes without spoiling what was coming in the updates. This didn't mean there was an update to the game each week, but for me it meant that I had something to look forward to and I think it somewhat made me more patient for updates. Now I don't know why, but for StS2 it's now getting almost comical how expectations are managed. First, the info is scarce but also not centralized. I know discord is a thing, but why am I learning about the next update taking more time than expected from a discord comment and not directly on the platform where I bought the game? This information should be posted right here on Steam. Second, I don't like how cryptic the communications are. It's always a "We can't say anything, but you'll see! It's going to be big!" and then I'm left to wait a month to be told to wait maybe another one, who knows? I know the devs don't owe me anything. It is their game and they update it like they want. But I feel they could be managing expectations a little better. You don't want to update each week? Fine. I get that. You think you need many months to build a cool update. That's fine too! Take all the time you need. That's not the problem. The problem is expectations. The second I saw that darkened preview of a new enemy in the newsletter I knew this meant that it would only be revealed in the next monthly one, which meant the update was not coming for another month at least, but the devs won't say it. No, you have to guess it! I don't know about the other players, but each friday that I look for an update or at least a post about progress, I feel crushed when there is none. For me, knowing how good I had it with Factorio, it just makes me realize how this company may be good at making great games, but not as good at managing the expectations of their players.

author: reynal2_omnicide
text:
Ironclad power fantasy of being "strong" is not fulfilled...
I played Ironclad in STS1 and the new ironclad is not even a shadow of its former self. Without ways of scaling in cards like limit break (doubles strength), reaper (heals damage done to enemies), and most importantly HEAVY BLADE!! [damage gained by strength is multiplied x3 (x5 upgraded) per strength]. Strength feels unrewarding and pointless. Not only that, but all the bad powers (aggression, juggernaut, and juggling) contaminating its card pool mean you can never pick powers. Even when "good powers" like dark embrace or feel no pain show up, they become curses and unpickable if you have no synergies going the moment you pick them up. Sometimes you build your deck based on specific synergies in early game, hoping for a power that will bring the deck together. Ex, perfected strikes and pommel strikes for the entire game since early game for hellraiser to never show up. Or exhaust based decks for dark embrace or feel no pain because the power pool has too many useless options. Can we make bloodletting common again? ty. Maybe make conflagration uncommon to make up for the lack of HEAVY BLADE.

author: AlenaFenomena
text:
Accessibility
Hiya! I enjoyed StS especially because it has an Esperanto localization, but I had a Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) diagnosis between then and now. I was wondering if it would be possible to have a setting where the graphics flashing and motion could be toggled or reduced? The game would be just as playable without them, and it would enable people to play who have visual sensitivities to motion. There are very few video games I can play now. Parallax is the worst headache inducer for me (both irl and in-game) so it's always exciting to find a fun game which doesn't require parallax to make the basic game mechanics work! But I haven't bought StS2 yet, because I the amount of graphic motion (cards swiping, attacks, etc) is still too much. My symptoms are very typical for head injuries. Protect yer noggins, folks! Turns out that multiple Non-TBI head injuries can add up to TBI status in the end.

author: dracos12
text:
Living Fog is a pretty ridiculous normal
https://slaythespire2.gg/enemies/living-fog I last played them on ascension 0 before the most recent balance patch, but honestly the nerf to bombing wouldn't have mattered. What in the world made it a good idea to have an 80 hp act 1 enemy that basically disables Skills at no action cost to itself for the entire fight? Not even an elite like Gremlin Nob, but just a random enemy? Nob sacrifices a turn and only gives a dangerous penalty even, not just free 'hey after turn one, only one skill a turn'. I had what had been looking like a really fun start with Necro. Most my strikes had gotten milled, some of my defends too. Most my added cards added extra 0 cost skills... oh wait. Suddenly I'm in a spot where a third of my deck makes things worse for me by filling my deck with more unplayable cards, a defend/soul/doom setup with rapid osty circulation suddenly is a huge disadvantage, since encountering something like that with an 80% skill deck that generates more skills is instantly run ending. I literally couldn't do a thing most turns, since act 1 defends generally aren't 17+ defend for 1 card. And reading its nerf, it still would've cleaned the clock of a deck that probably would've easily cruised all the way to end game otherwise. Overall, I feel too much mechanic shutdown stuff seems to be slipping into the game. Not punish mechanic, but just shut it off. Seeing that stuff on random enemies that aren't even elite is particularly ridiculous. At least when the parasite elite punishes thin decks, it is a challenge you could choose to dodge (by dodging elites) and is intended as an extra dangerous encounter. Writing this really hoping the devs consider more 'punishing' or 'doing damage' to builds rather than 'shut this down'. I left my last few runs miserable, and my wife did the same with the runs before... which is just surreal as we'd played a lot of the prior game and I was coming off a 10-long clear the whole game streak in STS 2 across every character. The enemy could've done a TURN of skill nerf and had a turn of adding it back in it's rotation, instead of 'attack, double attack, attack, double attack' while your skills are locked down. Genuinely felt like a 'are you playing ironclad with rage? No? Well sucks to be you.' I can't imagine it ends up fun with necro or silent ever.
